modified_caption: The line plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and different measures of Accuracy (Final Accuracy, ∆ Accuracy, Initial Accuracy). The x-axis represents 'Initial Confidence' on a linear scale, ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01 except that 0.87 is missing. The y-axis represents 'Accuracy,' also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The blue line, representing 'Final Accuracy,' uses circle markers and a solid line style. It starts at approximately 0.9 and steadily increases to reach 1.0 at the highest confidence level. The orange line, denoting '∆ Accuracy,' features diamond markers and a dashed line style, beginning near 0.3 at 0.86 and showing a sharp decline to below 0.05 at 0.95, before stabilizing at around 0.1. The green line, indicating 'Initial Accuracy,' uses square markers with a dashed line style. It starts at about 0.65, showing a gradual increase to around 0.95 before plateauing at the highest confidence level. All three lines include error bars, indicating variability at each data point. The Final Accuracy consistently exceeds Initial Accuracy across all confidence levels, as shown in the plot.

modifications.claim: The blue line (Final Accuracy) steadily increases to reach 1.0 at the highest confidence level.
modifications.reality: The blue line remains consistently high around 0.9 across the x-axis and does not steadily increase to 1.0.

modifications.claim: The orange line (∆ Accuracy) shows a sharp decline to below 0.05 at 0.95 before stabilizing at around 0.1.
modifications.reality: The orange line declines slightly to around 0.10 at 0.95 and fluctuates slightly afterward, finishing around 0.2. It does not drop below 0.05 or stabilize at 0.1.

modifications.claim: The green line (Initial Accuracy) plateaus at the highest confidence level.
modifications.reality: The green line decreases slightly at the highest confidence level instead of plateauing.
